text.p: Online book retailer Amazon.com has raised the price of shares in its initial public offering, due later this week, to between $14 and $16 each, according to lead underwriter Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
It originally planned to offer shares between $12 and $14.
Amazon.com also will offer three million shares, up from its original filing of 2.5 million.
The change means Amazon will be able to raise $45 million in its Wall Street debut. It originally estimated it would raise $32.5 million.
The IPO is due to price "mid to later this week", according to the lead underwriter. Analysts are expecting a rise of ten percent or more at its market debut.
